news.text: PLTR fell ~8.4% today, extending a 2026 rotation out of richly-valued AI/software names (the "SaaSpocalypse") as investors demand concrete AI monetization proof; trailing P/E is near 144x.
Microsoft and Amazon pushing into data-ontology/AI-orchestration is a growing competitive threat to Palantir's commercial pricing power, per recent coverage.
Q2 earnings due Aug 3 with the stock down ~30-40% YTD; options are pricing a large post-earnings swing, and bulls (Oppenheimer, Citi ~$200 targets) see a beat-and-raise as a thesis reset.
SOFI reports Q2 earnings before the bell tomorrow (Jul 29); analysts expect EPS $0.11 (+37.5% YoY) and revenue +30% to $1.11B.
Stock trades well below the average analyst target of $20.63 heading into the print, though Street sentiment leans Hold (6 buy/9 hold/3 sell).
NYSE issued a non-compliance notice on 7/24 after SRFM's 30-day average close fell below $1 — no immediate delisting impact, but a real risk to keep watching.
Wheels Up signed as launch customer for SurfOS Enterprise BrokerOS (up to $12M subscription revenue) and Surf Air expanded its Palantir partnership, leaning into a software/aviation-OS story.
April refinancing cut convertible notes from ~$47M to ~$16.9M and added a new term loan plus an aircraft-backed credit facility, improving liquidity.
FY26 Q4 revenue beat huge: $258.7M vs. ~$95M estimate (+407% YoY), adjusted EPS +$0.04 vs. an expected loss, and ~$20.2B of new long-term contracted lease revenue was added.
GAAP net loss of $110.6M ($0.39/share adjusted) was wider than the $0.09 loss expected, and total debt sits near $5B against $4.2B cash — financing risk persists despite the beat.
Stock whipsawed after the print and is extending gains again today as the market weighs the huge backlog against ongoing cash burn.
No material company-specific news found today; SERV's ~5.8% drop reads as broad-market/sector weakness rather than a new negative catalyst.
Company is prioritizing efficiency and margin improvement over expansion ahead of Aug 6 earnings, including a new laundry-delivery pilot to diversify revenue.
RSI briefly exited oversold territory in mid-July before sliding back to 28 as of the latest close — still a volatile, unprofitable name.
An FDA advisory panel backed 6 of 7 compounded GLP-1/peptide products reviewed, fueling a retail-driven rebound after the prior week's 14% single-day plunge.
Stock is still down ~19% for July even after the bounce; Q2 earnings due Aug 10 with consensus modeling a steep ~-141% YoY EPS decline as the compounding-pharmacy mix shifts.
A $400M receivables facility (early July) and a BofA price-target hike to $36 point to improving liquidity and Street optimism on weight-loss drug momentum.
Q2 beat-and-rally continues: subscription revenue +24.5% YoY, non-GAAP operating margin near 30%, and AI now over $1B in annual contract value.
49-analyst consensus is Strong Buy with a 12-month target of $140.25 (~31% upside from current levels); next earnings has rolled to ~Oct 28.
FQ4 earnings due tomorrow (Jul 29) after the close; consensus calls for $87.71B revenue (+15% YoY) and $4.24 EPS, with Azure growth above 40% the key swing factor.
Morgan Stanley reiterated Overweight with a $600 target, arguing Azure beating guidance by even 1pt would improve the market's read on AI ROI.
S&P Global downgraded Oracle to BBB- (lowest investment-grade tier), citing weak free cash flow (-$23.7B in FY26) and elevated AI-capex business risk.
Management plans to raise ~$40B in FY27 via debt and equity, including an already-announced $20B at-the-market share offering — a real dilution/financing overhang.

Shares are down ~28% over the past month on OpenAI-concentration and financing fears even as cloud (OCI) growth stays strong; Street's average target of $268 implies well over 100% upside if the balance-sheet worries don't materialize.

A securities-fraud class action was filed after Z/ZG stock fell ~16-17% on allegations of an anticompetitive listing agreement with Redfin; a federal judge has already rejected Zillow/Redfin's motion to end the related FTC suit.
Analyst targets were cut this month — Keefe Bruyette to $37, Jefferies to $60 — reflecting the litigation overhang and housing-market caution.

recommendations.rationale: Earnings tomorrow; Azure growth is the key bar
Up 83% from cost basis; consider partial trim
132% upside to analyst target despite debt fears
S&P downgrade to BBB-; $40B raise planned
Securities fraud suit over Redfin listing deal
Cloud giants entering PLTR's data-ontology turf
Backlog hits $20B; growth outpacing cash burn
Earnings Aug 3; deep AI-software selloff backdrop
Earnings Aug 6; largest position by weight
Earnings Aug 10; steep EPS decline expected
Earnings Aug 11; NYSE compliance risk too

ORCL's RSI moved to 32.97 (from 26.86 Friday) on Monday's bounce, so it no longer meets the <30 oversold threshold today; flagged instead as add-consideration given the large gap to analyst target.

Support/resistance and analyst targets are carried from the weekly-cache snapshot (refreshed 2026-07-20, now 8 days old - within the 10-day freshness window but approaching it; will need a refresh within 2 days).

Sector field is newly introduced this run (no prior classification existed); all 10 positions were freshly classified this run and should be reused verbatim by future runs unless the underlying business changes.

News search was run for all 10 positions this run per the all-positions-every-run policy; SERV, SOFI, and SERV's efficiency-pilot item reflect the most recent material coverage found even though no fresh catalyst emerged today.

PLTR's -8.4% drop is portfolio's biggest mover; no single-company catalyst was identified beyond broader AI-software valuation rotation ('SaaSpocalypse') and competitive-threat commentary - flagged as a risk-change given the competitive dynamic, not just a one-day price move.
